Fixed-effects count regression

Source: R/countreg_fe.R
countreg_fe.Rd

Estimates count regression models with fixed effects for one or more grouping variables (sites, years, ...). Poisson models use the conditional likelihood (one fixed-effect dimension) or IRLS with alternating projections (several dimensions); other families, including families made with new_count_family(), use the dummy-variable likelihood with the group effects concentrated out.

Usage

countreg_fe(
  formula,
  fixef,
  data,
  family = "POISSON",
  offset = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  method = c("auto", "conditional", "demean", "concentrated"),
  stderr = c("cluster", "hessian"),
  cluster = NULL,
  jackknife = FALSE,
  time = NULL,
  max.iters = 1000,
  tol = 1e-10,
  keep_data = TRUE,
  sp = NULL
)

Arguments

formula

model formula of the mean, y ~ x1 + x2, with an optional offset(). The intercept is absorbed by the fixed effects.

fixef

a one-sided formula of the fixed-effect variables, e.g. ~ site or ~ site + year.

data

a data frame.

family

the count family: "POISSON" (default) or any other family of countreg() (one fixed-effect dimension; enter further dimensions with few levels, such as years, as factors in formula), or a family made with new_count_family().

offset

optional name of an offset column (or use offset() in the formula).

weights

optional name of a column of frequency weights.

method

"auto" (default: "conditional" for Poisson with one dimension, "demean" for Poisson with several, "concentrated" otherwise), or one of those.

stderr

"cluster" (default; cluster-robust by cluster) or "hessian".

cluster

the clustering variable(s) for stderr = "cluster": a one-sided formula, column name(s) or a vector (see vcov.flexCountReg). The default is the first fixed-effect variable. Clusters must contain whole groups of that variable.

jackknife

logical: apply the split-panel jackknife bias correction of Dhaene and Jochmans (2015) to the slopes (for families other than Poisson in short panels). Each group's observations, ordered by time, are split into a first and second half (sharing the middle period when the number of periods is odd); the corrected estimate is \(2\hat\theta - (\hat\theta_1 + \hat\theta_2)/2\), for the slopes and the distribution parameters.

time

optional column that orders the observations within groups for jackknife (default: the row order).

max.iters

maximum number of iterations.

tol

convergence tolerance (relative change of the log-likelihood or of the deviance).

keep_data

logical; store the data in the fit (needed for predictions on the training rows without newdata).

sp

optional fixed smoothing parameters for smooth terms in formula; by default they are selected automatically.

Value

An object of class c("countreg_fe", "flexCountReg"). model$fixef holds the estimated effects of each dimension, model$dropped the groups and rows that were dropped, and model$not_identified the regressors without variation within groups.

Details

Poisson fixed-effects estimates of the slopes are consistent with fixed T and need only a correct conditional mean (Wooldridge 1999). For other families the concentrated (dummy-variable) estimates have an incidental-parameter bias of order 1/T. For NB2 the bias of the slopes is small (Allison and Waterman 2002), but the dispersion is strongly underestimated in short panels. In simulations with 200 groups (NB2, size 2), the bias of ln(alpha) was -1.08, -0.55 and -0.24 with T = 3, 5 and 10 periods, and slope biases were 1-2\ jackknife = TRUE reduced the dispersion bias to -0.03 (T = 5) and 0.06 (T = 10) but did not improve the slopes, and it failed with T = 3 (its half-panels are too short; a warning is given below 4 periods). The conditional negative binomial of Hausman, Hall and Griliches is a different model (its fixed effect enters the dispersion) and is not provided.

Standard errors are cluster-robust by the first fixed-effect variable by default, with the factor \(G/(G-1)\) for \(G\) clusters. They equal those of fixest::fepois() and fixest::fenegbin() with ssc(adj = FALSE); by default fixest also multiplies the variance by \((n-1)/(n-K)\). The log-likelihood is that of the dummy-variable model, and its degrees of freedom count the fixed effects, so AIC and BIC compare with models that estimate them.

Smooth terms. formula may contain smooth terms (s(x), te(), ...) of variables that change within groups; a smooth of a variable that is constant within groups is absorbed by the fixed effects and gives an error. The fit is then penalized, with the smoothing parameters selected as in countreg(). The smooth bases are built on the rows used in estimation (after dropping all-zero and single-observation groups), so with fixed smoothing parameters the estimates equal those of mgcv::gam() with group dummies. The jackknife is not available with smooth terms.

predict() uses each known group's estimated effect. A group not in the estimation data has no fixed effect: its prediction is NA, unless newgroup = "mean_fe" is given to use the weighted mean of the estimated effects.

References

Allison, P.D. and Waterman, R.P. (2002). Fixed-effects negative binomial regression models. Sociological Methodology, 32, 247-265.

Correia, S., Guimaraes, P. and Zylkin, T. (2020). Fast Poisson estimation with high-dimensional fixed effects. The Stata Journal, 20(1), 95-115.

Dhaene, G. and Jochmans, K. (2015). Split-panel jackknife estimation of fixed-effect models. Review of Economic Studies, 82(3), 991-1030.

Wooldridge, J.M. (1999). Distribution-free estimation of some nonlinear panel data models. Journal of Econometrics, 90(1), 77-97.

Examples

# \donttest{
data("washington_roads")
fe <- countreg_fe(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + offset(lnlength),
                  fixef = ~ ID, data = washington_roads)
#> 804 row(s) in 273 group(s) with all-zero counts or a single observation were dropped: they carry no information on the slopes.
summary(fe)
#> Call:
#> countreg_fe(formula = Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + offset(lnlength), 
#>     fixef = ~ID, data = washington_roads)
#> 
#> Model: countreg_fe | family: POISSON | optimizer: conditional
#> Poisson fixed effects (conditional likelihood) 
#> Groups dropped (all-zero counts or one observation): 273 
#> Iterations: 4 
#> Convergence: converged 
#> 
#> Coefficients (standard errors: cluster-robust (234 clusters of ID)):
#>        Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
#> lnaadt   -0.543      0.491    -1.1     0.27
#> Offset: offset(lnlength) (coefficient fixed at 1)
#> 
#> Log-likelihood: -735.347 | AIC: 1940.695 | BIC: 3009.189 
#> N: 697 | panels: 234
# }
